title: Blush Flower Tassel Ornament
subtitle: A layered crochet flower with two leaves on a beaded cord
finished_size: ≈ 21 cm (8.3 in) plus an 8 cm loop
description: A flat layered flower — yellow centre, six pink petals and six large cream petals worked on chain loops behind them — with two small leaves below, strung on a beaded cord above a cream tassel.
glance: ≈ 21 cm (8.3 in) plus an 8 cm loop
size_guide: One size. For a larger ornament use light worsted (#4) cotton and a 3 mm hook; for a smaller one use sport-weight cotton and a 2 mm hook. Beads and tassel length can be changed freely.
gauge: 22 sc and 24 rows/rnds = 10 cm (4 in) in single crochet with a 2.5 mm hook. Gauge is not critical for an ornament, but work firmly so that stuffing does not show and flat pieces keep their shape; sizes depend on your tension.
swatch: Optional density check: ch 12, then work 10 rows of sc on 11 sts. The square should measure about 5 cm (2 in) wide and 4 cm (1.6 in) tall. If it is larger or you see gaps between stitches, use a smaller hook.

materials.detail: DK (#3) cotton, cream — approx. 14 m (15 yd), about 6 g — 1 ball of 50 g (about 115 m) is enough
DK (#3) cotton, blush pink — approx. 3 m (4 yd), about 2 g — 1 ball of 50 g (about 115 m) is enough
DK (#3) cotton, sage green — approx. 3 m (4 yd), about 2 g — 1 ball of 50 g (about 115 m) is enough
DK (#3) cotton, mustard yellow — approx. 3 m (4 yd), about 2 g — 1 ball of 50 g (about 115 m) is enough
5 gold-tone beads 6 mm (hole at least 2.5 mm); 2 natural wooden beads 12 mm (hole at least 3 mm). Both cord strands must pass through each bead together — test before you start.
tapestry needle, stiff card for the tassel, scissors

techniques.name: Magic ring (MR)
techniques.how: Wrap the yarn twice around two fingers, insert the hook under both strands, pull up a loop and ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). Work the stitches of Rnd 1 over both strands, then pull the tail firmly to close the centre.

techniques.name: Working in the back bumps of a chain
techniques.how: Turn the chain over: each chain has a small horizontal bar (the back bump) on the back. Insert the hook under that bar only. The front of the chain stays as a neat V edge, and later you can work along the other side of the chain into the remaining loops.

techniques.name: Tassel neck wrap
techniques.how: Lay a 5 cm loop of the wrapping strand along the tassel, pointing down. Wrap the long end tightly around tassel and loop, from the top down. Pass the end through the loop, then pull the short tail at the top until the loop disappears under the wraps. Trim both ends and hide them in the skirt.

notes: Terms: US crochet terms are used throughout; UK makers: US sc is the UK double crochet.
Stitch counts: the number in parentheses at the end of a row or round is the number of stitches you have when it is finished. Tick the box when you finish each step.
Spiral rounds (magic-ring pieces with no "Join"): do not join or turn; mark the first stitch of each round and move the marker up.
Joined rounds (the round says "Join"): unless the round says otherwise, start with ch 1 (does not count as a stitch) and finish with a sl st into the first stitch.
Rows: ch 1 at the end of a row, before turning, does not count as a stitch.
Right side: for pieces in rounds, the outside of the rounds; for pieces in rows, choose the neater side and mark it. "Wrong sides together" means the marked right sides face out.
Tails: leave a 20 cm (8 in) tail on pieces that will be sewn; weave in all other ends as you go.

items: Read Before You Begin and gather the beads; check that both cord strands pass through every bead.
Make the tassel and tie the hanging cord into it (Tassel).
String beads and pieces on the cord, tie the knot and the hanging loop (Assembly & Finishing).

sections.title: Flower
sections.kicker: Yarns D, B and A · make 1

blocks.text: The flower is worked in joined rounds: a yellow centre, a ring of six pink petals, then a round of chain loops behind them that carries the six large cream petals.

steps.label: Rnd 1
steps.text: With Yarn D, 6 sc in MR. Join.

steps.label: Rnd 2
steps.text: inc x6. Join and fasten off Yarn D.

steps.label: Rnd 3
steps.text: Inner petals: join Yarn B with a sl st in any st. *(sc, hdc, dc) in next st, (dc, hdc, sc) in next st*; rep from * 5 more times. Join with a sl st to the first sc. Fasten off Yarn B.

steps.label: Rnd 4
steps.text: Petal base loops, worked behind Rnd 3: fold the pink petals forwards. Join Yarn A with a sl st around the post of a Rnd 2 st at the gap between two petals. *Ch 5, sl st around the post of the Rnd 2 st at the next gap between petals*; rep from * 5 more times, the last sl st in the first sl st.

steps.label: Rnd 5
steps.text: Outer petals: in each ch-5 loop work (sc, hdc, 2 dc, tr, 2 dc, hdc, sc). Join with a sl st to the first sc and fasten off.

steps.label: Leaf
steps.text: Leaving a 20 cm starting tail, make a chain of 7. Working in the back bumps: sl st in 2nd ch from hook, sc in next ch, hdc in next ch, dc in next 2 ch, 3 sc in last ch; working along the other side of the chain: dc in next 2 ch, hdc in next ch, sc in next ch, sl st in the last ch (the tip). Ch 2, sl st in 2nd ch from hook (tiny point). Fasten off and weave in this end.

blocks.text: Place the two leaves with their 3-sc bases touching and the tips pointing down and outwards (an upside-down V). Sew the bases together over 5 mm with the starting tails.
Make the tassel when the crochet pieces are finished. The hanging cord is tied into its top, so it runs up through the whole ornament and is anchored in the tassel.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.text: Cut a piece of stiff card 9 cm (3.5 in) tall. Wrap Yarn A (cream) around the card 40 times, keeping the wraps side by side and not too tight. Cut the yarn at the bottom edge.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.text: Cut the hanging cord: one 110 cm (43 in) length of Yarn A. Slide it under all the wraps along the top edge of the card so that its middle sits there, and tie it in a tight square knot around the wraps. Both cord ends now point upwards.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.text: Cut through all the wraps along the bottom edge of the card and remove the card. Let the strands hang down from the cord knot.

steps.label: Step 4
steps.text: Tassel neck: cut a 70 cm length of Yarn A. Measure 2 cm down from the top fold and wrap it tightly 8 times around the bundle (see Tassel neck wrap in Techniques).

steps.label: Step 5
steps.text: Trim the skirt evenly to 8 cm (3.1 in) from the top fold. Hold it over steam (or dampen it) and comb the strands straight with your fingers; let it dry hanging.

items: Thread both cord ends together through a large-eye tapestry needle (or a bead needle with a big eye). Work upwards from the tassel.
String, from the tassel upwards: 1 gold bead → 1 wooden bead → 1 gold bead → the leaves → 1 gold bead → the flower → 1 gold bead → 1 wooden bead → 1 gold bead.
Leaves: pass the needle up through the sewn bases of the two leaves.
Flower: enter at the base of the lowest outer petal, run the needle up behind the stitches on the back, through the centre, and out at the top of the highest outer petal.
Push everything down snugly onto the tassel so there are no gaps. Holding both cord ends together, tie one overhand knot right above the top bead to lock the stack.

Hanging loop: tie the two cord ends together with a square knot so that the loop measures 8 cm (3 in) from the overhand knot to the top. Trim the ends to 5 mm and add a drop of fabric glue to the knot if you like.

blocks.label: Safety
blocks.text: This is a decoration, not a toy, and not suitable for children under 3 years. Beads and cords are a choking and strangling hazard: hang it out of reach of babies, young children and pets.
Count your stitches at these points; the numbers match the rows above.

items: One stitch too many or too few: check the last increase or decrease round, and that you did not work into the slip-stitch join or the ch 1 at the start of a row.
Piece cups or ripples: your tension differs from the gauge; change hook size by 0.25–0.5 mm rather than the stitch counts.
Stuffing shows through: use a smaller hook, or stuff a little less firmly.
Flat pieces curl: pin them out, mist with water (or starch) and let them dry flat.
Cord will not pass through a bead: thread one strand at a time with a fine needle, or use beads with larger holes.

accuracy.text: Sizes are scaled from the photo using the 12 mm wooden beads as the reference; the photos look like rendered images, so stitch counts are a design reconstruction, not a count from a real sample. Make the piece once and compare before selling the pattern.

assumptions: Petal stitch groups are a design choice that gives the photographed petal sizes.
